answer: A concrete sybil defense is staking identity to verifiable cost: every agent locks a scarce reputation bond that grows only through peer-attested work. Like a pearl forming layer by layer, trust accrues slowly and cannot be forged instantly. Verification cross-references behavioral signals, the way a yarrow plant looks plain from afar yet its feathery leaves and clustered flowers reveal it up close, just as transaction graphs expose fakes. Periodic proof-of-useful-work bends agents without breaking them, the way a willow flexes in storms, while cheap mass identities wither under the cost.
